title: 5.2.0 Update
description: Zones, captions, doors, Japanese and Chinese, and pictures pasted straight onto the map.

changes.message: Zones: the rectangle in Shapes is now a zone. It colours only the map's floor inside it, so a room is tinted without covering walls, and two zones that cross keep one even colour. Zones you already placed look this way too.
Captions: right-click any placed item and choose Create caption to leave a note on it. Hover the marker to read it, and choose whether captions print in screenshots and video.
Icarus now comes in Japanese and Simplified Chinese. It opens in your system's language, and Settings has a Language section to pick another.
Doors on Lotus, Summit and Ascent open and close with a click, each page keeps its own, and view cones stop at a shut door. Replays show the doors too.
Harbor's High Tide now draws its wall. Drag the handles to bend it and set where it ends.
Paste a picture straight onto the map with Ctrl+V.
View cones gain a full circle, and Settings has a slider for how strongly cones light the floor.
Hold Alt while dragging to snap an item onto the map's walls and floor edges.
Right-click a page to rename or delete it, and a placed agent to delete it. A circle or view cone can be taken off an agent without deleting the agent.
Rectangles grow up to 110 m on both sides. Cyber Cage and Hot Hands are drawn at their in-game size.
Importing a strategy, archive or backup puts it in the folder you have open, in your local library or in the cloud.

Cloud saving is more dependable on a poor connection. Edits made while a save is still on its way are kept, the save button shows what is true, and Icarus asks you to sign in again when your session has ended.
A screenshot or video now waits for its pictures to load, so an export no longer comes out missing them.
Items dropped near the edge of the map are no longer deleted, and an item dropped under a side panel comes back into view.
A drag box selects everything it touches, not only what sits fully inside it.
Exports you rename keep their file type, and a file opens as what it holds, whatever it is named.
Menus, buttons and loading move faster and more evenly, and only one right-click menu shows at a time.
